doc.title: Richard Wyands interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

chapter: Growing up in the Bay Area
title: Drum lessons with Johnny Otis and junior high drumming
summary: He took up drums, studied with Johnny Otis, and played in school bands but found carrying drums a chore.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: So by the time you were going into high school you kind of had a direction?

Well I don’t know. I ran into a road block in junior high school I decided I wanted to be a drummer. And I’d already been playing classical music and a little jazz. And for some reason — oh my cousin was a drummer, and he loaned me some of his drums and my parents weren’t too happy about that idea but I took lessons, actually I took lessons from Johnny Otis, who lived in the neighborhood.

Johnny Otis. At that time his name was Johnny Veliotes. And I went to school with his younger brother, but I studied with him. And he was a very good drummer before he decided to be a band leader. All right. I played drums in junior high school, I played in the orchestra, the band, the marching band, and the director, he liked me especially because being a pianist and I studied, I was a better reader, a little bit better sight reader than the other drummers so he gave me the choice I was the number one drummer.

No. I had to play a whole set of drums — plus I played in a dance band too, a junior high school dance band, which is kind of interesting. I didn’t own a set of drums, my parents said no, we’re not going to buy you a set of drums, forget it. So I had to use the school drums and I had to use one of these big street drums as a bass drum, I had a foot pedal that was a heel pedal, heel.

And I thought it was glamorous, you know the girls were all smiling and everything. But later I found out being a drummer wasn’t so great after all because at the end of the dance I’m trying to take down the drums and everything, in the meantime everybody’s going, musicians and everyone is gone and I’m still fooling around with these drums. I had to carry them all the way across the school yard, so I don’t know about this.
The piano is starting to look good again.
